_what_this_is: Pixel reftests: a page, and assertions about what it must look like.
Run by `make render-conformance` (tools/conformance/render_check.py),
which reads the PNG with its own decoder so the engine is not asked to
grade its own writer.
An assertion is one of:
pixel      a point is a colour (tolerance optional, 0 by default)
rect       a rectangle is uniformly a colour
uniform    a rectangle is one colour, whichever it is
not-colour a point is anything but a colour
differs    two points are not the same colour (something was painted)
Coordinates are CSS pixels from the top left of the 800x600 viewport.
Exact equality is the default on purpose: box edges here are not
anti-aliased, so an off-by-one is a bug rather than a rounding.
A test may carry `known_failure`: a sentence saying what the spec requires
and the engine does not do yet. The run prints KNOWN with the reason, and
counts it as neither a pass nor a failure. The entry is a debt, not a
silence: if the page starts passing, the run prints FIXED and exits 1, so
the reason has to come out in the same commit that fixes the bug.
Phase 180 cleared the earlier known failures; Phase 193 added one for
inline white-space:nowrap failing to prevent replaced-element wrapping.

tests.name: svg_shapes_paint_where_getbbox_says
tests.html: <!doctype html><html><head><style>html{background:#fff}body{margin:0}svg{display:block}</style></head><body><svg width="200" height="120"><rect x="10" y="10" width="40" height="30" fill="#ff0000"/><circle cx="100" cy="25" r="15" fill="#0000ff"/><path d="M20 100 A40 40 0 0 1 100 100" fill="#00ff00"/></svg></body></html>

assert.describe: the rect's fill is where its x/y/width/height put it
the circle's centre is its cx/cy
the arc M20 100 A40 40 0 0 1 100 100 rises exactly 40 user units from its chord -- the rim of the circle the sweep follows, which is the curve bound getBBox() reports

nothing is painted outside the shapes
